citation: Roesel et al. 2021, Bowel function recovery after laparoscopic transverse colectomy within an ERAS program
design: prospective-database retrospective comparison within standardized ERAS
population_or_comparison: 126 patients: segmental transverse colectomy 20, right colectomy 65, left colectomy 41
field_signal_or_operation_detail: elective laparoscopic segmental transverse colectomy versus right/left colectomy; exact mesocolic and vascular steps not fully extracted
poi_ppoi_result: PPOI 25% TC, 40% RC, 24% LC; TC lower than RC (OR for RC versus TC 4.255, 95% CI 1.092-16.667)
field_resolution: moderate for operation category; low for named structures
signal_class: positive for field/extent distinction; counter-signal against transverse location alone
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: segmental transverse surgery does not behave like right colectomy for PPOI; supports studying the actual field and extent rather than tumor segment alone

citation: Milone et al. 2019, Short- and long-term outcomes after transverse versus extended colectomy for transverse colon cancer
population_or_comparison: transverse colectomy versus extended hemicolectomy for transverse colon tumors
field_signal_or_operation_detail: direct comparison of conservative transverse resection and extended resection; structure-level technique not uniformly extractable from abstract
poi_ppoi_result: abstract reports no statistical difference in overall short-term outcomes; ileus-specific pooled estimate not available in abstract
field_resolution: low-moderate for comparative outcome; low for structures
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: shows that extended versus segmental transverse surgery does not produce a uniformly reproducible short-term harm signal across all studies

citation: Milone et al. 2020, Mid-transverse colon cancer and extended versus transverse colectomy: SICO CCN multicenter collaborative study
population_or_comparison: 1529 mid-transverse cancer patients: segmental resection 388, extended resection 1141
field_signal_or_operation_detail: mid-transverse tumor; extended right or left hemicolectomy versus segmental resection; detailed field components require full text
poi_ppoi_result: overall complications 30.1% segmental versus 23.6% extended; first flatus, first mobilization and LOS were statistically shorter in the extended group; ileus-specific result not given in abstract
field_resolution: moderate for extent comparison; low-moderate for structures
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: does not support a simple monotonic extent-to-POI rule; selection, approach, anastomosis and field composition require reconstruction

citation: de'Angelis et al. 2021, Extended right colectomy, left colectomy, or segmental left colectomy for splenic flexure carcinomas
field_signal_or_operation_detail: splenic-flexure region; progressive extension of resection compared across ERC, LC and SLC
poi_ppoi_result: operative time, time to flatus, time to regular diet and LOS increased with extension; ERC had higher postoperative ileus risk than LC and SLC
field_resolution: moderate for extent comparison; low for individual structures
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: supports the idea that greater anatomic resection/field extension can associate with ileus, but this is a splenic-flexure control region rather than proof of the hepatic-flexure/transverse mechanism

citation: Cao et al. 2024, Short- and long-term outcomes after surgical treatment of 5918 patients with splenic flexure colon cancer
population_or_comparison: 5918 splenic-flexure cancer patients across extended right, segmental and left colectomy studies
field_signal_or_operation_detail: splenic-flexure cancer; extended right versus left and segmental approaches
poi_ppoi_result: five studies with 958 patients reported ileus; ERC versus LC OR 2.34 (95% CI 1.28-4.30); no heterogeneity reported for this comparison
field_resolution: moderate for pooled outcome; low for individual structures
signal_class: replicated extension-associated ileus signal in an anatomic control region
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: strengthens the general proposition that extended field/resection can matter, while leaving open whether the same applies to hepatic-flexure/transverse operations

citation: Popescu et al. 2022, Extended lymphadenectomy for proximal transverse colon cancer: Is there a place for standardization?
population_or_comparison: 43 proximal transverse colon cancer cases, all treated with CME, high vascular ligation and GCLN lymphadenectomy
field_signal_or_operation_detail: explicit GCLN stations No. 204, 206 and 214v; operative figures show stomach, pancreas, middle colic vessels and GCL; median operation time 180 min
field_resolution: high for defining the proximal transverse/GCLN operative field; no dysmotility endpoint
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: provides the most explicit operative anatomy for the proximal transverse/GCLN field and can define future extraction fields, but cannot itself establish POI/DGE risk

citation: Sun et al. 2023, Comparing the techniques and outcomes of laparoscopic transverse colectomy to laparoscopic hemicolectomy in mid-transverse colon cancer resection
population_or_comparison: 70 mid-transverse cancer patients: transverse colectomy 40, hemicolectomy 30
field_signal_or_operation_detail: segmental transverse colectomy versus right/left hemicolectomy; transverse mesocolon retraction and mesenteric lymph-node dissection described; caudal-to-cephalic versus cephalic-to-caudal transverse approaches compared
poi_ppoi_result: overall postoperative complications 20.0% transverse versus 40.0% hemicolectomy (P=0.067); one paralytic ileus requiring an ileus tube occurred in the extended-right group; recovery times comparable
field_resolution: moderate for operation category and transverse mesocolon handling; low for middle-colic-root/GCLN details
signal_class: counter-signal supporting specific-field rather than generic-transverse interpretation
interpretation_for_current_hypothesis: segmental transverse resection with mesenteric dissection can have equal or lower short-term morbidity than hemicolectomy; the risk signal may depend on which additional structures are entered
